verification.notes: Changed since the previous review (f6ca6a89de796213): the lifecycle/audit lesson was rewritten into delegated access, SSO, webhooks and audit, keeping a retention and deletion section. Sources fetched 2026-10-22: OAuth 2.1 is at draft 16 (Sept 2026), omits implicit and password grants, requires code_challenge unless 7.5.1.1 (confidential client plus OIDC nonce assurance) holds, requires exact redirect matching and says clients MUST NOT send access tokens in a query parameter; RFC 9700 says the password grant MUST NOT be used, implicit SHOULD NOT, public clients MUST use PKCE, and tokens SHOULD be restricted to minimum privilege and one resource server; RFC 6749 recommends at most ten minutes for codes; RFC 7636 defines S256 as BASE64URL(SHA256(verifier)). SAML Core 3.2.2 requires the recipient to check Destination; SAML Profiles 4.1.4.3 requires Recipient, NotOnOrAfter and InResponseTo checks and 4.1.4.5 requires keeping used assertion IDs until NotOnOrAfter (PDF text extracted locally with pdfjs). OIDC Core 3.1.3.7 matches the iss/aud/signature/exp/iat/nonce rows. The OWASP SAML sheet says to ignore KeyInfo, validate Destination, Recipient, InResponseTo, audience and time, and detect replay at response or assertion level. Standard Webhooks 1.0.0 matches the headers, signed content, v1 prefix, space-separated list, constant-time comparison and the re-serialization warning. OWASP Logging matches when/where/who/what, authn/authz failures and the data-to-exclude list. The 600-second replay-key arithmetic is correct. No human or external independent approval and no full-catalogue acceptance is claimed.
